coverage_claim: WM-ACT-054 covers one source-qualified research subject-to-study participation aggregate from candidate identification through screening, permission, enrolment, allocation, actual participation, safety, exit, protected data and specimen use, correction, retention and projection. Candidate containment, research-type and jurisdiction profiles, ethics and privacy review, release-pinned mappings and independent external review remain deferred.

boundary_decision.rationale: The subject composes independently identifiable identifier bindings, screening events, eligibility decisions, permission sources, enrolment and allocation events, activities, state transitions, safety links and withdrawal assertions over one subject-to-study relationship. Aggregate is more accurate than person, study or event. The frozen record_plane world-model and catalogue entry_kind standalone-mm are separate axes.

decisions.concept: Participation versus subject and study masters
decisions.rationale: The aggregate owns one study-specific participation relationship. Person or other subject and Research Study remain external masters.
Human, animal, specimen, product, device, group, household and organization participation have different identity, ethics and lifecycle semantics and require explicit profiles.
Recruitment, contact, prescreening, screening, eligibility, permission, enrolment, allocation and participation are distinct source-qualified processes, events or decisions.

External repositories own source artifacts and validity. Participation owns scoped, versioned bindings and independently records consent, assent, representative permission, refusal, reconsent and withdrawal.
Planned arm, assigned group, allocation concealment, actual exposure, adherence and protocol deviation remain independent assertions.
Withdrawal from intervention, participation, future contact, data use and specimen use have separate scopes; retention or disposition follows permission, protocol, law, ethics and records policy.
Pseudonymization and de-identification do not establish anonymity. Linkage, re-identification, disclosure and direct-identifier views remain protected and purpose-bound.
The incoming WM-ACT-036 CONTAINS WM-ACT-054 relation remains candidate. It supports a parent study reference but grants no protocol ownership, mutation or cascade behavior.
FHIR R5, CDISC ODM and CDASH, WHO TRDS and ClinicalTrials.gov cover different scopes and maturity levels. Every mapping must pin version, profile and information loss.

One Claude Sonnet and one Grok 4.6 research attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex audited the frozen validated result and comparison locally without tools or new research facts. Confidence remains medium and assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok 4.6 research attempt for WM-ACT-054 each timed out after 120 seconds. No external research result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-ACT-036 CONTAINS WM-ACT-054 remains candidate and grants no ownership, mutation or cascade behavior.

Research-profile hold: human clinical, observational, behavioral, public-health, device, animal, specimen, product, group and other research require explicit subject, ethics and jurisdiction profiles.

Ethics and privacy hold: eligibility, consent, representative authority, safety, compensation, re-identification, data and specimen use, disclosure and retention require adopting-Dimension and jurisdiction policies.
Interoperability hold: all FHIR, CDISC, WHO and ClinicalTrials.gov projections require release-pinned mappings, maturity and scope constraints, information-loss declarations and validation.
Source-access hold: ISO 14155:2026 normative text and detailed CDISC files were not publicly inspected; claims from them are limited to official public metadata.
